plan_title: Amended Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan Campo Viejo Plant Pozo Acido Viejo No. 1 Esperanza No. 1 Yoakum County, Texas
ama_definition: Same boundary as the MMA, on the grounds that the only probable leakage paths are penetrating wells and surface equipment; it contains the plume through year 55 (p46).
mma_definition: The modeled plume 25 years after injection ends (about 3,337 acres, 1% gas saturation cutoff) plus a buffer of at least half a mile (p44-45).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Existing wells penetrating the injection zone are rated 'possible' with medium magnitude (six offset penetrations); surface equipment is remote but monitored; drilling, faults, confining zone and seismicity are remote or very unlikely (p46-48).
baseline_summary: Injection volume and pressure measurements taken before the original 2022 plan was implemented, plus a 2022 baseline sample from the on-site water well; 2023 and 2024 samples reported no variance (p68-69).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 of the following year; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data or to report monitoring results to the state is stated in the plan text (p73, p76).

rows.detail: Volumetric flowmeter on injected stream, compiled quarterly; composition from continuous analyzer or representative sampling, averaged quarterly; monthly gas composition collected for both AGI wells; separate meter for any future stream.
rows.location: Injection stream upstream of the AGI wellheads; new RR meter in service Q4 2025
rows.evidence_quote: Flowmeters will be continuously operated except for maintenance and calibration.

rows.detail: SCADA and distributed control system continuously record injection volume and pressure at both AGI wells; wellhead pressure gauges, high/low pressure shut-in valve, and set points to keep pressure below fracture gradient.
rows.location: Pozo Acido Viejo No. 1 and Esperanza No. 1 wellheads; plant surface equipment
rows.trigger_or_response: Data outside limits or deviation suggesting fault/seal pathway: alert, field review, shut in wells if needed; M3.0+ seismic event triggers review of volumes and pressures.
rows.evidence_quote: Stakeholder continuously monitors and collects injection volumes and pressures through their SCADA systems

rows.detail: Pressure gauge on the casing annulus of each AGI well; a change in annulus pressure is treated as a sign of a possible leak.
rows.location: Casing annulus of both AGI wells
rows.trigger_or_response: Change in annulus pressure indicates possible leak; reviewed under response procedures.
rows.evidence_quote: a pressure gauge on the casing annulus. A change of pressure on the annulus would indicate the presence of a possible leak.

rows.detail: Annual MITs under TRRC rules to confirm the AGI wells and wellheads hold pressure.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT: review MIT data, volumes and pressures; if AGI stream leakage is likely, isolate the well and mitigate.
rows.evidence_quote: Mechanical integrity tests (MITs) required under TRRC rules are run annually

rows.detail: Daily field inspections of the plant and both AGI wells, looking at gauges, monitors and leak signs such as vapor plumes and ice; well inspections listed as 'as needed'.
rows.location: Campo Viejo Facility and the two AGI well sites
rows.trigger_or_response: Vapor clouds or ice found: corrective action taken.
rows.evidence_quote: field personnel conduct daily visual field inspections of gauges, monitors, and leak indicators, such as vapor plumes.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors alarming at 10 ppm; H2S is the proxy for CO2. Monitoring table lists frequency as 'As needed'.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, check monitors, secure facility; CO2 release quantified from operating conditions.
rows.evidence_quote: all Stakeholder field personnel are required to wear H2S monitors, which trigger the alarm at 10 ppm.

rows.detail: Fixed H2S detectors (10 ppm alarm) around plant and AGI wells; H2S and CO2 monitoring at well sites; CO2 monitors at any new meter; handheld CO2 readings near penetrations at least quarterly.
rows.location: Plant, AGI well sites; identified penetrations within the MMA/AMA
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, verify monitor, secure facility.
rows.evidence_quote: The H2S gas detectors, located around the facility and the well site, trigger alarms at 10 ppm.

rows.detail: Water well(s) on the facility property (about 180 ft deep) sampled yearly and analyzed by a third-party lab.
rows.location: Water well(s) on the Campo Viejo facility property
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant change in water analysis: investigate whether it came from AGI well leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: sampling the wells on the facility property and analyzing the samples with a third-party laboratory on an annual basis

rows.detail: Operator-installed seismic station near Campo Viejo, tied into TexNet; plan also cites a one-time USGS and TexNet catalog review.
rows.trigger_or_response: Event of M3.0 or greater: review AGI injection volumes and pressures for signs of leakage; quantify any leak.
rows.evidence_quote: Stakeholder has installed a seismic monitoring station near Campo Viejo.

rows.detail: Risk table cites a past regional seismic evaluation finding no faults in the confining or injection zones; no repeat seismic planned.
rows.evidence_quote: A regional seismic evaluation did not identify any faulting of the confining or injection zones

rows.detail: At least quarterly atmospheric CO2/H2S monitoring near identified penetrations, described elsewhere as periodic hand-held monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: as well as minimum, quarterly atmospheric monitoring near identified penetrations within the MMA.

rows.detail: Corrosion control program checked by periodic inspection of the system and of the cathodic protection system.
rows.evidence_quote: The effectiveness of the internal and external corrosion control program is monitored through the periodic inspection of the system

rows.detail: H2S monitoring during offset drilling operations, listed for the drilling-through-the-MMA pathway.
rows.location: Offset drilling operations in the MMA
rows.evidence_quote: H2S monitoring during offset drilling operations

rows.detail: Subpart W methods for equipment between meter and wellhead; detected leaks quantified from operating conditions or case-by-case engineering analysis, reservoir modeling and history matching; blowdowns go to flare.
rows.location: Surface equipment between flowmeter and wellhead
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak detected: quantified, addressed and documented.
rows.evidence_quote: Calculation methods from Subpart W will be used to calculate CO2 emissions caused by any surface leakage

notes: Amendment adds Esperanza No. 1 (permit pending at time of writing) and replaces Estacado No. 1, now shut in. Appendix pages with the step-rate test and the Pozo Acido Viejo UIC order/GAU letter are image-only (p81-85, p91-95), so permit monitoring conditions could not be checked. Personal H2S monitors listed 'As needed' in Table 11; frequency coded unspecified. Quarterly handheld CO2 'atmospheric monitoring' near penetrations coded under fixed_gas_detectors, not atmospheric_co2. 'Regional seismic evaluation' (p47) may refer to reflection seismic or seismicity review; unclear.
